text:
A concerning document exposed in recent weeks shows how far the Population and Immigration Authority is prepared to go in its push for expanded surveillance powers. The document outlines PIBA's request to hire the intelligence company PenLink to supply advanced monitoring tools – including location tracking, large-scale social media analysis, and AI-driven profiling systems.

Yesterday, 17.5.26, the Israeli Association for International Couples, together with the Privacy Law Clinic at Tel Aviv University and the Association for Civil Rights in Israel, sent a formal demand to the Ministry of Finance, PIBA, and the Attorney General’s Office calling to block this move.

At stake is not only abstract policy, but everyday life. These tools are explicitly intended to analyze “routine deviations,” map relationships, and build detailed profiles on individuals – including citizens, migrants, asylum seekers, and international couples whose lives already undergo intense scrutiny.
